sentences.en: From NPR, this is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 来自NPR，这里是《隐藏的心智》。

sentences.en: There is so much in our culture that celebrates the power of positive thinking.
sentences.zh: 我们的文化中有很多赞美积极思维力量的内容。

sentences.en: We're often told to follow our hearts, to dream big.
sentences.zh: 我们经常被告知要跟随内心，敢于做大梦。

sentences.en: You can have, do, or be anything you want.
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有、做到或成为你想成为的任何人。

sentences.en: Whatever belief you hold in your subconscious mind will become your reality.
sentences.zh: 你在潜意识中所持有的任何信念都会成为你的现实。

sentences.en: Value yourself and believe in yourself.
sentences.zh: 重视你自己，相信你自己。

sentences.en: Because believing that the dots will connect down the road will give you the confidence to follow your heart,
sentences.zh: 因为相信未来的点点滴滴会串联起来，会给你跟随内心的信心，

sentences.en: even when it leads you off the well-worn path.
sentences.zh: 即使它引领你离开那条循规蹈矩的路。

sentences.en: But now, researcher Gabrielle Etienne says, maybe we should all dream a little smaller.
sentences.zh: 但现在，研究员加布里埃尔·艾蒂安表示，也许我们都应该把梦想做小一点。

sentences.en: Positive fantasies and daydreams, as pleasurable they are,
sentences.zh: 积极的幻想和白日梦，尽管它们令人愉悦，

sentences.en: they have a problem when it comes to fulfilling our wishes and attaining our goals.
sentences.zh: 但在实现我们的愿望和达成目标方面，它们有一个问题。

sentences.en: Today, as part of our You 2.0 series, we bring you an episode from our archive that asks,
sentences.zh: 今天，作为我们“你2.0”系列的一部分，我们为您带来归档中的一期节目，探讨一个问题：

sentences.en: is there a methodical way to achieve your dreams?
sentences.zh: 有没有一种有条不紊的方法来实现你的梦想？

sentences.en: And this scientific technique has an acronym.
sentences.zh: 而这项科学技术有一个缩写。

sentences.en: Gabrielle is a professor at New York University,
sentences.zh: 加布里埃尔是纽约大学的一名教授，

sentences.en: and author of the book, Rethinking Positive Thinking, Inside the New Science of Motivation.
sentences.zh: 也是《重新思考积极思维：探寻动机的新科学》一书的作者。

sentences.en: She's from Germany, and she said growing up, no one told her to shoot for the stars.
sentences.zh: 她来自德国，她说在成长过程中，没有人告诉她要志存高远。

sentences.en: The idea of big dreams, big hopes, was, if at all, more implicit than explicit.
sentences.zh: 宏大梦想、宏大希望这种概念，如果有的话，也更多是含蓄的，而非显性的。

sentences.en: When she came to the United States, though, Gabrielle noticed a real cultural difference.
sentences.zh: 然而，当她来到美国时，加布里埃尔注意到了一种真正的文化差异。

sentences.en: Well, when I came to America, it was wonderful, because people always said,
sentences.zh: 嗯，当我来到美国时，这太棒了，因为人们总是说，

sentences.en: yes, do it, yes, that's possible, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的，去做吧，是的，那是可能的，对。

sentences.en: Okay, this is a good idea, why don't you do it?
sentences.zh: 好吧，这是一个好主意，你为什么不去做呢？

sentences.en: Whereas back in Europe, people were more cautious and said, you know,

sentences.en: are you sure you want to do this?
Are you sure this is possible?
So, I was really happy to come to America,

sentences.zh: 因为人们只是在某种程度上鼓励你的任何想法。

sentences.en: So yes, positive thinking, indulging in fantasies about the future, does feel good.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，积极思维，沉溺于对未来的幻想中，确实感觉很好。

sentences.en: But when Gabrielle started to research this topic, she found something interesting.
sentences.zh: 但当加布里埃尔开始研究这个课题时，她发现了一些有趣的事情。

sentences.en: Well, these positive fantasies, they seduce us to feel already accomplished,

sentences.en: and they take our energy away.
